author: Jay
name: PZAdmin
short: Project Zomboid server status, restarts, mod requests and status dots in channel names via PZAdmin.
description: Shows Project Zomboid server status and who is online, lets approved users trigger a graceful restart, and lets players request mods for the server tied to the channel they're in. It can also put a 🟢 / 🔴 at the start of a channel's name to show whether a server is up. The bot only talks to PZAdmin's HTTP API; PZAdmin does the RCON, container and mod work itself.
install_msg: Set up with [p]pzadminset url <pzadmin url> (e.g. http://192.168.0.50:27815), then DM the bot: [p]set api pzadmin api_key <key>. Check it with [p]pzadminset show. For slash commands: [p]slash enable pz, [p]slash enable pzctl, then [p]slash sync. The key needs the control scope for restarts. Lock down restarts with [p]permissions setdefaultglobalrule deny pzctl, then allow specific users with [p]permissions addglobalrule allow pzctl <user>. For mod requests: give the key the request scope, link each server's channel with [p]pzadminset link #channel <server>, then [p]slash sync again so /pz request shows up. Requests wait in the Requests section of the server's Mods tab in PZAdmin. For status dots in a channel's name: give the bot Manage Channels on the channel, then [p]pzadminset dots add #channel [server]. Don't also turn on PZAdmin's own "Show 🟢 / 🔴 in the channel's name" option for that channel: both bots would rename it and use up Discord's limit of two renames every ten minutes.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores which channels belong to which server and which show its status. Mod requests send the requester's Discord username and ID to your PZAdmin, which keeps them with the request.
